score_suite_design_findings: Public SCORE rubric defines anchors only for 1, 3, and 5.
Curated gold uses intermediate expected scores 2 and 4 although those anchors are not defined.
All four SCORE cases use score_tolerance=0.25, requiring near-exact absolute scoring despite under-specified intermediate anchors.
The SCORE calibration set contains only four distinct cases, so rank and absolute-score metrics are sensitive to a small number of judgments.
audit_interpretation: J3r1 shows systematic downward absolute-score calibration rather than broad label or pairwise failure.
J1 and J3r1 independently reached the same Spearman value 0.948683 while both failed the absolute MAE threshold.
These observations justify auditing rubric/gold/threshold methodology; they do not justify changing thresholds or gold to make either candidate pass.
required_next_actions: Do not search additional Judge candidates until the calibration methodology is audited.
Do not tune gold labels or thresholds from J1/J3r1 errors.
Independently define explicit semantic anchors for scores 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.
Re-annotate SCORE cases with independent human ratings and adjudication, recording disagreement before setting tolerance.
Set absolute-score tolerance and qualification thresholds from the audited rubric and human disagreement, not from model outcomes.
Revisit SCORE sample size before another formal Judge qualification.
label_pairwise_status: NO_METHODOLOGY_CHANGE_PROPOSED_FROM_J3R1; retain unless independent audit finds a separate issue.
